title: Generic constancy of numerical data of contracted nodal components
statement: Let $T$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $(X,D)$ and $(Y,E)$ be multipointed $T$-curves [def-trf-multipointed-curve], and let $f_X:Y\to X$ and $f_D:E\to D$ be compatible proper $T$-morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose that for every $t\in T$, after passing to an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre], every nonsmooth point of $Y_\Omega$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is an ordinary node, meaning its completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $E_t$ is etale over $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and lies in the smooth locus of $Y_t$. For each reduced irreducible component $R$ of $Y_\Omega$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] whose image under $(f_X)_\Omega$ is one point, $R$ is proper over $\Omega$. Associate to it the triple $(p_R,a_R,b_R)$: $p_R=\dim_\Omega H^1(R,\mathcal O_R)$, using Zariski sheaf cohomology [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]; $a_R$ is the number of self-nodes, namely ambient nodes whose two branches both belong to $R$; and $b_R$ is the number of DISTINCT points of $R\cap(E_\Omega\cup\operatorname{Sing}(Y_\Omega))$, where $\operatorname{Sing}$ denotes the nonsmooth locus. These numbers and the number of contracted components are finite. There is a nonempty open subset $T^\circ\subseteq T$ such that the finite multiset of triples $(p_R,a_R,b_R)$ over all contracted components is the same for every $t\in T^\circ$ and every choice of $\Omega$. The empty multiset is allowed. Neither $Y\to T$ nor $X\to T$ is assumed proper or separated, and no generic-isomorphism or modification hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), proof, printed p. 34, contracted-component weighted incidence data; take only generic constancy, retain loops, and decorate the graph with markings and incidences with noncontracted components. This numerical refinement is agent-stated. The proof there invokes EGA IV3 13.1.3, 9.7.9, 9.7.12, 11.1.1 and EGA III2 7.6.9. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-contracted-component-no-extra-generic] to $Z=Y$, $W=X$ and $h=f_X$. The family hypotheses follow from [def-trf-multipointed-curve] and the assumed nodal geometric fibres; no modification hypothesis is needed. It proves properness of every contracted reduced component in every geometric fibre, and gives a nonempty affine $U\subseteq T$, a finite etale surjective integral affine $S\to U$, component families $H_i\subseteq Y_S$, and a fixed contracted sublist $J$. Each geometric fibre of $H_i$ is exactly one reduced irreducible component, and the generic fibre $H_{i,\xi}$ is proper when $i\in J$. Pull back the marked source to $S$ using [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change]. The marking remains a closed immersion with etale fibres in the smooth locus. The families $H_i/S$ are at this point only flat and finitely presented; no assertion that $Y_S/S$ is proper is made.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion for generic constancy of the weighted contracted-component data, with distinct marked/ambient-singular incidences. The properness-of-closure step uses Stacks Tag 081F.

proof.text: For every $i\in J$, prove properness of $H_i$ after shrinking $S$, rather than assuming ambient properness. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ a Noetherian domain. The schemes $H_i$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; finite presentation also makes them quasi-compact. The principal opens $S_b=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/b]$, for $0\ne b\in B$, have affine transitions and limit $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]: the directed colimit of the rings $B[1/b]$ is $\operatorname{Frac}B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper] to $H_i\to S$ in this system, with $X_0=H_i$ and $Y_0=S_0=S$. All three schemes are qcqs, the morphism is locally of finite type, and its limit is the proper generic fibre from Step 1. Thus $H_i\times_S S_{b_i}\to S_{b_i}$ is proper for some nonzero $b_i$. The product of the finitely many $b_i$ is nonzero. Restriction to its principal open makes all contracted component families proper simultaneously, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. If $J$ is empty take this open to be $S$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion for generic constancy of the weighted contracted-component data, with distinct marked/ambient-singular incidences. The properness-of-closure step uses Stacks Tag 081F.

proof.text: For $i\in J$, apply [lem-trf-contracted-component-generic-spread] with ambient marked family $(Y_S,E_S)$ and supplied component family $H_i$ over the open from Step 2. Its properness input is exactly $H_i/S$, now proved; its flatness, finite presentation and geometric-component condition are supplied by Step 1. On a further nonempty open, this fixes $p_i=\dim H^1(H_{i,\bar s},\mathcal O)$, the self-node count $a_i$, and the number $b_i$ of DISTINCT marking/ambient-singular incidence points. Apply this successively to the finite list, using proper base change to retain properness on later restrictions. This gives a nonempty open $V\subseteq S$ where every triple is fixed. There are no numerical conditions to impose if $J$ is empty. The same spread lemma also proves the finiteness clause of the item at an arbitrary geometric fibre, even outside $U$: apply it over the one-point integral base $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $H=R$ and ambient pair $(Y_\Omega,E_\Omega)$. Step 1 gives properness of $R$; over a field it is flat and finitely presented, and it is a reduced irreducible component by construction. The only nonempty open of this base is the whole base. Finiteness of the component list follows from the enumeration statement applied to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion for generic constancy of the weighted contracted-component data, with distinct marked/ambient-singular incidences. The properness-of-closure step uses Stacks Tag 081F.

proof.text: Return to the original base by setting $T^\circ=U\setminus\pi(S\setminus V)$. The complement $S\setminus V$ has its reduced closed-subscheme structure. Its composite map to $U$ is finite: over an affine open it is the quotient of the finite algebra defining $S$. Hence its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. Because $S$ is integral and finite dominant over integral $U$, its generic fibre is the spectrum of the single field $\kappa(\eta_S)$, a finite field extension of $\operatorname{Frac}B$; its unique point maps to the generic point of $U$. That point belongs to $V$, so this closed image misses the generic point of $U$. Thus $T^\circ$ is a nonempty open of $T$, and $S\times_U T^\circ\subseteq V$ still surjects onto $T^\circ$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34; agent expansion for generic constancy of the weighted contracted-component data, with distinct marked/ambient-singular incidences. The properness-of-closure step uses Stacks Tag 081F.

proof.text: For $t\in T^\circ$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(t)$, choose a point of the nonempty finite etale fibre $S_t$ and embed its finite separable residue extension into $\Omega$. This gives a geometric lift $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$. The geometric fibre $Y_{\bar s}$ and its marking and map are the original $Y_\Omega,E_\Omega,(f_X)_\Omega$, by the fibre-product identities. Step 1 therefore identifies its contracted components, each exactly once, with the $H_{i,\bar s}$ for $i\in J$. Step 3 assigns these components the fixed triples $(p_i,a_i,b_i)$. Consequently the multiset is the fixed multiset indexed by $J$, independent of $t$, the lift and $\Omega$. When $J$ is empty it is the empty multiset. This argument descends the multiset, not individually labelled geometric components.

split_report.summary: Repair of E1: generic component families are first enumerated on an integral finite etale cover; Stacks 081F, applied to each contracted component closure in the principal-open inverse system, proves properness of that closure after shrinking. The numerical spread lemma then takes this proper closure as input in a possibly nonproper ambient curve. A finite closed-image argument descends the resulting open and multiset to T. Restored the current main statement verbatim: the previous repair had added an eta-modification assumption which is neither needed for this generic-data lemma nor preserved on the closed strata used by its parent. Both retained new nodes are statement-only, with no ambient properness or generic-isomorphism assumption.
